brief.headline: No metal traded in London this weekend, so the aluminium price is unchanged at about $3,274 a tonne, but three separate pieces of weekend news - cheaper oil and gas, reports that Iran and Oman are close to a deal on shipping through the Gulf, and a clear increase in the supply of the raw materials used to make aluminium - all point to lower costs and less scarcity ahead.
bullets: NOTHING MOVED, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO SAY. The London Metal Exchange is closed at weekends, so there is no new price today. The figures on this page are Friday's: aluminium at about $3,274 a tonne for metal you take now, and about $3,250 for metal in three months' time. Friday's drop of roughly two percent was caused by American inflation figures, not by anything to do with aluminium - every metal on the exchange fell the same day.

THE ONE ENCOURAGING SIGN FROM FRIDAY IS STILL STANDING. Metal for immediate delivery is still more expensive than metal for later delivery, by $24 a tonne, and that gap barely moved even though the price fell sharply. When people pay extra to get metal now, it usually means real buyers are short of it. That said, the signal has not been tested for three days now, so it should not be read as getting stronger.

ENERGY AND GEOPOLITICS BOTH EASED OVER THE WEEKEND. Oil fell to about $105 a barrel and European gas to about EUR 80 a megawatt hour - both of which lower the cost of running a smelter, since electricity is the single biggest expense in making aluminium. Separately, Iran said on 7 September that an arrangement with Oman on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is only days away, after a temporary route was agreed in late August. The waterway has not reopened and no deal has been signed, but the risk of supply being cut off there now looks lower than it did.

THE RAW MATERIALS ARE GETTING MORE PLENTIFUL, NOT LESS. A dated industry analysis published on 12 September reports bauxite shipments from Guinea up 28% on a year earlier, forecasts for next year's bauxite prices well below this year's, alumina exports from Asia up 27% in the first half, and India's alumina surplus nearly four times bigger than a year ago. WHAT TO WATCH: Monday's exchange price - and whether that $24 premium for immediate metal survives - then the US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday 16 September.

drivers.text: THE GULF-SCARCITY PILLAR UNDER EVERY WESTERN PREMIUM ON THIS PANEL WEAKENED AGAIN, AND THIS TIME THE EVIDENCE IS DIPLOMATIC RATHER THAN COMMERCIAL — Regional premiums outside China are underwritten by two assumptions: that Gulf metal is scarce, and that Gulf routes are unreliable. BOTH WERE CONTRADICTED THIS WEEK BY DIFFERENT SOURCES. On the commercial side, an 11-September market review states that outside China production resumptions and new ramp-ups continued, that DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED, and that supply outside China kept repairing. On the routing side, dated reporting of 07-September has Iran saying an agreement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping is days away, with a temporary route already agreed in late August. THE QUALIFICATION IS CARRIED RATHER THAN DROPPED: the waterway will not fully reopen until the United States fulfils commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed, and no deal is signed. A PREMIUM IS A PRICE FOR SCARCITY AND UNCERTAINTY; BOTH JUST GOT CHEAPER.
drivers.source: Bloomberg, 07-September-2026 - Iran says Strait of Hormuz deal with Oman just days away

drivers.text: THE US ROWS ARE STILL MOSTLY TARIFF, AND THE DECOMPOSITION IS RECOMPUTED EVERY RUN SO THE TWO LEGS CAN BE READ APART — Section 232 stands at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, re-verified this run, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. The tariff leg is levied on value, so it moves with the LME whether or not anything physical changes. AT THE CARRIED CASH OF $3,274.00 THE TARIFF LEG OF A US DUTY-PAID TONNE IS $1,637.00, AND AGAINST THE CARRIED US DUTY-PAID ASSESSMENT OF $2,094/t THAT LEAVES AN IMPLIED MARKET LEG OF $457.00. Friday's $69 fall in the benchmark cut the tariff leg by $34.50 and MECHANICALLY WIDENED the apparent market leg by the same amount - an 8% apparent strengthening of the US physical premium caused by nothing physical whatsoever. THAT IS THE NUMBER TO REMEMBER WHEN A US PREMIUM HEADLINE SAYS THE MARKET TIGHTENED. Canada's counter-tariffs, in force since 08-September at 50% across $27.6bn of imports and 300-plus metals products, compound the distortion in the other direction.
drivers.source: Westmetall - LME official cash settlement, 11-September-2026 board (both language versions, cross-checked)

drivers.text: THE COST SIDE OF THE PREMIUM ARGUMENT IS LOOSENING FASTER THAN THE METAL SIDE, WHICH IS A MARGIN STORY RATHER THAN A PREMIUM STORY — A dated 12-September industry analysis records Guinean bauxite shipments of 4.33 Mt in the 21-27 August week, up 3.7% week on week and 28.4% year on year; 2026 Guinea FOB bauxite forecast at USD 34-46 per dry metric tonne against USD 40-65 in 2025; Australian FOB bauxite at USD 39.15 per wet metric tonne in FY26 against USD 51.48 in FY25; Asian alumina exports of 7.05 Mt in H1-2026, up 27.36% year on year; and India's alumina trade surplus nearly quadrupling to 1.72 Mt. NONE OF THIS IS A PREMIUM INPUT DIRECTLY - PREMIA ARE PAID FOR DELIVERED METAL, NOT FOR ORE - BUT IT MATTERS TO THE PANEL BECAUSE IT REMOVES THE COST-PUSH JUSTIFICATION FOR HOLDING PREMIA UP. When the upstream is cheap and getting cheaper, a high regional premium has to be defended by physical scarcity alone, and the scarcity evidence is the part that weakened this week.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: THIS ROW IS DOWNGRADED FROM ESCALATING TO IMPAIRED-BUT-DE-ESCALATING, AND THE DOWNGRADE IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL JUDGEMENT ON THIS PAGE THIS RUN, SO THE EVIDENCE IS SET OUT IN FULL. DATED REPORTING OF 07-SEPTEMBER-2026 CARRIES IRAN SAYING AN AGREEMENT WITH OMAN TO MANAGE STRAIT OF HORMUZ SHIPPING IS DAYS AWAY, after more than three weeks of talks, with broad agreement on proposed inbound and outbound routes, technical arrangements covering the security and sovereignty of both states, and a proposed joint coordination centre to manage maritime traffic. A SEPARATE DATED REPORT OF 26-AUGUST-2026 STATES THAT A TEMPORARY MARITIME ROUTE HAD ALREADY BEEN AGREED. THREE QUALIFICATIONS ARE CARRIED RATHER THAN BURIED. FIRST, THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED: the same reporting states it will not fully reopen until the United States fulfils commitments under an interim deal signed in June THAT HAS SINCE LAPSED. SECOND, NO DEAL IS SIGNED - 'days away' has been said before in this conflict. THIRD, THE ESCALATION FACTS HAVE NOT BEEN DELETED: Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait and the United States said it retaliated by sinking five Iranian tankers, the worst fighting in months as the conflict nears seven months. THE REASON THIS PAGE MOVES THE TREND ANYWAY IS THAT THE ITEM HAS CHANGED CATEGORY: it was carried for weeks as a SINGLE UNCONFIRMED RUMOUR AT DELIBERATELY LOW CONFIDENCE, and it is now dated, specific and reported by more than one outlet. AN ARRANGEMENT THAT TIGHTENS IRANIAN CONTROL OVER THE WATERWAY IS NOT THE SAME AS A REOPENING, AND THAT AMBIGUITY IS WHY THE TREND MOVES ONE STEP RATHER THAN TO CLEAR.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: A SECOND CHOKEPOINT REMAINS IN PLAY AND NOTHING PUBLISHED THIS WEEKEND CHANGED IT. The Houthi group was reported to have seized the port city of Mocha, gaining leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure; Bab el-Mandeb transits are down about 24% since the July blockade and MARAD advisory 2026-006 runs to 22-September. THE IMPORTANCE IS ROUTING RATHER THAN VOLUME: Bab el-Mandeb is the alternative on which Hormuz-affected cargo has partly relied, so two contested chokepoints are not twice the risk of one - THEY REMOVE THE SUBSTITUTE. THAT LOGIC NOW RUNS IN REVERSE AND IT IS WORTH SAYING SO: if the Hormuz arrangement reported on 07-September completes, the pressure on Bab el-Mandeb as a substitute route falls at the same time, and the shipping-risk premium embedded in Western delivered prices unwinds from both ends at once. THE PHYSICAL CONTRADICTION ALSO PERSISTS: an 11-September market review reports Middle Eastern ingot supply into Japan as relatively ample and DAMAGED MIDDLE EASTERN CAPACITY AS RECOVERED.

headlines.title: THE WESTMETALL LANGUAGE DIVERGENCE HAS RESOLVED AND THE FIX WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. Both the English and the German overview boards were re-requested this morning and BOTH NOW CARRY THE 11-SEPTEMBER SESSION, identical line for line across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings. Yesterday German led and English lagged; on 04-August the positions were exactly reversed. THE OPERATING RULE IS NOW PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND IS UNCHANGED: neither language version of this source is reliable alone, the newer of the two is used, and the per-metal daily tables are the arbiter. THIS IS LOGGED AS MIXED RATHER THAN BULLISH BECAUSE A RESOLVED OUTAGE IS NOT THE SAME AS A RELIABLE SOURCE.

IRAN SAID ON 07-SEPTEMBER THAT A STRAIT OF HORMUZ ARRANGEMENT WITH OMAN IS DAYS AWAY, AND THIS PAGE TREATS THAT AS THE SINGLE LARGEST BEARISH ITEM IN FRONT OF THE ALUMINIUM MARKET. Reporting describes more than three weeks of talks, broad agreement on inbound and outbound routes, technical arrangements on the security and sovereignty of both states, and a proposed joint coordination centre; a separate report dated 26-August states a temporary maritime route had already been agreed. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED AND NO DEAL IS SIGNED - full reopening is reported as conditional on the United States fulfilling commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed. THE GULF CHOKEPOINT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE PILLAR UNDER WESTERN PHYSICAL PREMIA; A CREDIBLE PATH TO REOPENING IS A CREDIBLE PATH TO THOSE PREMIA COMPRESSING.

BAUXITE SUPPLY IS RISING AND FORWARD PRICE FORECASTS HAVE BEEN CUT ON BOTH MAJOR ORIGINS. A dated 12-September analysis records Guinean shipments of 4.33 Mt in the 21-27 August week, up 3.7% week on week and 28.4% YEAR ON YEAR, even as some suspended Guinean mines continued to stockpile at port with no near-term plan to resume. GUINEA FOB BAUXITE IS FORECAST AT USD 34-46/dmt FOR 2026 AGAINST USD 40-65/dmt IN 2025; AUSTRALIAN FOB AT USD 39.15/wmt IN FY26 AGAINST USD 51.48/wmt IN FY25. Delivered cost rather than FOB is becoming the operative benchmark as freight and ore quality do more of the work. BEARISH FOR THE ALUMINA COST CURVE AND THEREFORE FOR THE COST FLOOR UNDER THE METAL PRICE - BUT CONSTRUCTIVE FOR SMELTER MARGIN, AND THOSE ARE NOT THE SAME TRADE.

ASIA EXPORTED 7.05 Mt OF ALUMINA WORTH USD 2.76bn IN H1-2026, UP 27.36% YEAR ON YEAR, AND INDIA HAS SWUNG DECISIVELY TO THE EXPORT SIDE. Indian alumina exports rose 51.3% to 2.5 Mt while imports fell 34.9% to 775,362 t, taking the country's alumina trade surplus to 1.72 Mt - NEARLY QUADRUPLE A YEAR EARLIER. Whether Asia reaches 8 Mt of H2 shipments is described as depending on geopolitical disruption, refinery capacity and demand. A REGION FLIPPING FROM NET IMPORTER TO LARGE NET EXPORTER CHANGES WHERE THE MARGINAL TONNE IS PRICED, WHICH IS A STRUCTURAL CHANGE RATHER THAN A CYCLICAL ONE, and it sits awkwardly beside the flat $353.50/mt FOB East Australia print of 11-September.

THE JAPANESE Q4 PRODUCER OFFER OF USD 310-325/t FOR OCTOBER-DECEMBER SHIPMENTS, DOWN 18-22% ON THE USD 395/t Q3 SETTLEMENT, HAS NOW BEEN RESTATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER ON 12-SEPTEMBER. This page has carried that offer since a 02-September report naming Rio Tinto and South32 among the producers, with Japanese buyers targeting below USD 300. THE CORROBORATION RAISES CONFIDENCE IN THE UPPER BOUND OF THE PENDING RANGE WITHOUT MOVING IT - the range stays at USD 280-310 because no NEWER dated input has printed and a range is not tightened on a repeated reading of the same evidence. A SETTLEMENT NEAR THE CONSENSUS LOW WOULD BE A FALL OF ROUGHLY 28% IN ONE QUARTER.

BRENT EASED TO USD 104.61 WITH THE DAY REPORTED AT -2.81% AND THE DIRECTION CORROBORATED BY THE SAME PUBLISHER'S OWN HEADLINE THAT THE RALLY PAUSED ON MIDDLE EAST DIPLOMACY; EUROPEAN GAS EASED TO EUR 79.52/MWh. THIS IS WHY THE BRENT DAY-CHANGE IS PUBLISHED THIS RUN AFTER BEING DELIBERATELY WITHHELD LAST RUN: the board's numeric change column is still unsigned and ambiguous, but an independent dated headline now fixes the sign. CHEAPER ENERGY LOWERS THE COST FLOOR UNDER THE MARGINAL SMELTER, WHICH IS BEARISH FOR PRICE AND POSITIVE FOR MARGIN. TAGGED MIXED FOR THAT REASON. The offset is the dollar index at 99.12, marginally firmer into a Federal Reserve decision on 16-September.

THE SUPPLY RESPONSE TO THE HIGH-PRICE REGIME IS NOW VISIBLE ACROSS FOUR SEPARATE ANNOUNCEMENTS AND ALL OF THEM ARRIVE LATE BY DESIGN. NALCO has signed a technology licensing agreement with Emirates Global Aluminium to deploy DX+ Ultra smelting technology at a proposed 500,000 t/y brownfield expansion at Angul, Odisha. Rio Tinto is acquiring the undeveloped Aurukun bauxite project from Glencore and Mitsubishi, potentially up to 8 million dry tonnes a year of export bauxite, adding to Weipa. Rusal is planning a bauxite and alumina complex in Indonesia with domestic partners. Ashapura is targeting 15 Mt of annual Guinean bauxite volumes by FY28. NOT ONE OF THESE ADDS A TONNE IN 2026, WHICH IS PRECISELY WHY THEY MATTER: THEY TELL YOU WHAT THE COST CURVE LOOKS LIKE IN 2029.

THE US DEPARTMENT OF WAR HAS COMMITTED A FURTHER USD 100 MILLION TO THE ATLANTIC ALUMINA COMPANY, TAKING TOTAL GOVERNMENT INVESTMENT TO USD 400 MILLION, TO PROTECT THE COUNTRY'S LAST REMAINING DOMESTIC ALUMINA REFINERY AS A DEFENCE SUPPLY CHAIN. IT IS TAGGED BULLISH DELIBERATELY AND THE REASONING IS WORTH STATING: state capital entering a market that every price signal says is in surplus is not a bet on the surplus - IT IS A STATEMENT THAT THE SURPLUS IS NOT TRUSTED TO PERSIST, AND THAT WESTERN REFINING CAPACITY IS NOW PRICED AS SECURITY RATHER THAN AS TONNES. Over a multi-year horizon it raises the floor under Western delivered costs by putting non-commercial capacity into the stack.

THE 11-SEPTEMBER MARKET REVIEW REMAINS THE MOST DIRECT CONTRADICTION OF THE GULF-SCARCITY CASE AND IT IS CARRIED FORWARD RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED BECAUSE NOTHING HAS SUPERSEDED IT. It states that outside China production resumptions and new capacity ramp-ups continued, that DAMAGED CAPACITY IN THE MIDDLE EAST RECOVERED, and that aluminium supply outside China kept repairing - alongside an earlier statement in the same week that Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan is relatively ample. IT IS UNCOMFORTABLE FOR THIS PAGE'S OWN BULL CASE, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT STAYS IN THE TOP HALF OF THE LIST. ITS EVIDENTIAL WEIGHT IS CAPPED: it is market commentary, not a production disclosure.

CANADA'S COUNTER-TARIFFS HAVE BEEN IN FORCE SINCE 08-SEPTEMBER AT 50% ACROSS USD 27.6bn OF IMPORTS AND 300-PLUS METALS PRODUCTS, AFTER US-CANADA TALKS COLLAPSED WITH A PROPOSED ALUMINIUM TARIFF CUT BRIEFLY ON THE TABLE. US Section 232 is re-verified this run and unchanged at 50% on articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. TAGGED MIXED BECAUSE THE TWO SIDES OF THE BORDER NOW PULL DELIVERED PRICES IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: the US duty raises the delivered cost of imported metal into the US while the Canadian counter-measure raises it going the other way, and the first measurable test is the next dated US Midwest assessment.

US PRIMARY ALUMINIUM PRODUCTION WAS 167,000 TONNES IN Q1-2026, UP 0.6% YEAR ON YEAR BUT 1.2% BELOW THE PRIOR QUARTER. THE NUMBER IS SMALL AND THAT IS THE FINDING. After a 50% Section 232 tariff, a completed Mt Holly restart to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and a Magnitude 7 Metals potline guided to start before year-end, the United States is still producing under 170,000 tonnes a quarter - a rounding error against roughly 4.5 million tonnes of quarterly Chinese output. TARIFFS HAVE MOVED PRICE FAR FASTER THAN THEY HAVE MOVED TONNES, WHICH IS THE CENTRAL FACT OF THE US MARKET AND IS BULLISH FOR US DELIVERED PRICES PRECISELY BECAUSE DOMESTIC SUPPLY CANNOT RESPOND.

THE STRUCTURAL SIGNAL FROM FRIDAY IS CARRIED UNCHANGED AND IS EXPLICITLY NOT UPGRADED. Flat price fell 2.06% on 11-September and the cash-to-three-month backwardation gave up ONE DOLLAR, from $25.00 to $24.00, while warehouse stock drew a fifth consecutive time to 244,100 tonnes. A FRAGILE FRONT-MONTH SIGNAL DOES NOT SURVIVE A TWO-PERCENT SELL-OFF INTACT - IT FLATTENS OR FLIPS - AND THIS ONE DID NEITHER, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE ON THIS PAGE THAT THE SELL-OFF WAS FINANCIAL AND UNRATIFIED BY THE PHYSICAL MARKET. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION IS THAT IT HAS NOW GONE THREE CALENDAR DAYS WITHOUT A TEST. Monday 14-September is the test, and the spread matters more than the price.

Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

catalysts.text: THE NEXT PUBLISHED LME OFFICIAL, DUE 13:20 LONDON, AND IT IS THE FIRST TEST OF THIS PAGE'S LEAD FINDING IN THREE CALENDAR DAYS. The question is not the flat price, it is the STRUCTURE. Friday's session cut flat price 2.06% and left the backwardation at $24.00 against $25.00. A SECOND AND THIRD SESSION IN WHICH THE FRONT STAYS FIRM WOULD CONFIRM THE SELL-OFF WAS FINANCIAL AND UNRATIFIED BY THE PHYSICAL MARKET; a flattening or flipping spread, or a material warehouse inflow, would say the opposite and would invalidate this page's lead finding outright. WATCH THE SPREAD AND THE STOCK LINE BEFORE THE FLAT PRICE.

US FEDERAL RESERVE DECISION - THE LARGEST SINGLE SCHEDULED EVENT IN FRONT OF THIS MARKET, NOW THREE DAYS OUT. The 11-September session was the market beginning to price it: August core consumer prices landed a tenth above forecast at +0.3% month on month, the dollar firmed, and the entire metals board fell in one session. THE DOLLAR INDEX IS FIRMER AGAIN AT 99.12. This event acts on aluminium through the dollar and through the discount rate applied to inventory financing, NOT through anything physical, which is why it can move the price without touching the curve.

RESOLUTION OF THE OCTOBER-DECEMBER ASIAN QUARTERLY PREMIUM. The pending range on this page is unchanged at $280-310 against a settled Q3 record of $395. It gained corroboration rather than movement this run: a second publisher on 12-September restates the $310-325/t producer offer as down 18-22% on Q3. THE NEWEST CONSENSUS OF $280-290 SITS BELOW THE PRODUCERS' OWN OFFER FLOOR, SO THE BURDEN OF CONCESSION IS ON THE SELLERS. A settlement at $285 would be a fall of roughly 28% in one quarter and would reset Asian delivered realisations for a full quarter.

COMPLETION OR COLLAPSE OF THE IRAN-OMAN STRAIT OF HORMUZ ARRANGEMENT. Iran said on 07-September that a deal was days away, following a temporary route reported agreed on 26-August. NOTHING IS SIGNED AND FULL REOPENING IS REPORTED AS CONDITIONAL ON LAPSED US COMMITMENTS. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-ASYMMETRY ITEM ON THE PAGE RATHER THAN THE HIGHEST-PROBABILITY ONE: the Gulf chokepoint underwrites the largest pillar of Western physical premia, and if it clears, the shipping-risk premium unwinds from BOTH chokepoints at once because Bab el-Mandeb's role as substitute route falls away simultaneously.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT CYCLE, NOW ABOUT FOUR DAYS AWAY. Prebaked anode and coal tar pitch settle monthly around the 17th-18th, and green petcoke settles on its own cycle. The current Sep-26 anode mark of ~5,730 and the 13-August pitch mark of ~4,960 are the live figures until then. CARBON IS THE SECOND-LARGEST VARIABLE COST IN A SMELTER AFTER POWER, so this is the next scheduled movement in the input basket and the next scheduled append to the basket's trend histories.

WHETHER THE UPSTREAM LOOSENING SHOWS UP IN A DATED ALUMINA PRICE. The quantity evidence is now unambiguous - Asian alumina exports up 27.36%, India's surplus quadrupled, Guinean bauxite shipments up 28.4% - but the most recent dated trade, $353.50/mt FOB East Australia on 11-September, was essentially flat on a five-week-old mark. IF THE NEXT DATED TRADE IS ALSO FLAT, THE SURPLUS IS BEING ABSORBED AND THE FALLING-COST THESIS IS WEAKER THAN THE VOLUME DATA SUGGESTS. That would be a genuine disconfirmation of a view this page has been building.

SLOVALCO'S GUIDED RESTART OF ITS FIRST 75,000 TONNES OF A 175,000-TONNE TOTAL, UNDER A SLOVAK CARBON-COST COMPENSATION AGREEMENT - NOW ROUGHLY TWO TO THREE WEEKS FROM ITS GUIDED WINDOW. It is the cleanest live test on this page of whether European smelting economics actually work at current power prices. European gas eased to EUR 79.52/MWh this run, which helps at the margin. A SLIPPED OR CANCELLED RESTART WOULD BE A LOUDER SIGNAL THAN A COMPLETED ONE.

THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT - about fifteen weeks away and the largest scheduled structural event on this page's horizon. The European duty-unpaid premium is the row most directly exposed. Europe must replace those tonnes and both candidate sources are constrained: Gulf metal sits behind the chokepoint question, and European restart capacity depends on power economics that have only just begun to improve. FIFTEEN WEEKS IS NOT LONG TO REROUTE A STRUCTURAL IMPORT FLOW.

risks.text: RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP ON UNCHANGED EVIDENCE, AND HOLDING IS A DECISION RATHER THAN INERTIA. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT TARIFF POLICY, NOT SUPPLY AND DEMAND, BECOMES THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE. No new tariff development printed this weekend, but the mechanism demonstrated on Friday is arithmetic and does not decay: Section 232 at 50% is levied on value, so at the carried cash of $3,274.00 the tariff leg of a US duty-paid tonne is $1,637.00 and the implied market leg against the unchanged $2,094/t assessment is $457.00. FRIDAY'S $69 FALL IN LONDON WIDENED THAT APPARENT MARKET LEG BY 8% WITH NOTHING PHYSICAL BEHIND IT. Canada's 50% counter-tariffs, in force since 08-September across $27.6bn of imports, compound it in the opposite direction, and 10-September reporting that US-Canada talks collapsed with an aluminium tariff cut briefly on the table means the regime is the residue of a failed negotiation - MORE LIKELY TO MOVE, NOT LESS.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP AND REINFORCED FROM A NEW DIRECTION. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT CURTAILED AND DISRUPTED CAPACITY RETURNS FASTER THAN THE MARKET EXPECTS. The 11-September market review stating that ex-China resumptions and ramp-ups continued and that DAMAGED MIDDLE EASTERN CAPACITY RECOVERED is carried forward, with its evidential weight still capped because it is commentary rather than company disclosure. WHAT IS NEW THIS RUN IS THE PIPELINE BEHIND IT: NALCO licensing EGA's DX+ Ultra for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion, Rio Tinto acquiring Aurukun at up to 8 Mdt/y of bauxite, Rusal planning an Indonesian complex, Ashapura targeting 15 Mt/y of Guinean bauxite by FY28. NONE OF IT LANDS IN 2026 AND THAT IS PRECISELY THE POINT - THE SUPPLY RESPONSE TO A HIGH-PRICE REGIME IS NOW VISIBLE AND DATED, WHICH MAKES THE REGIME HARDER TO SUSTAIN OVER THE HORIZON THE FORWARD CURVE ACTUALLY COVERS.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP, AND THE EVENT THAT DECIDES IT IS NOW THREE DAYS AWAY. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT MACRO TIGHTENING OVERWHELMS THE MICRO TIGHTNESS. The 11-September session converted this from forecast to realised: US August core consumer prices landed a tenth above forecast at +0.3% month on month, the dollar firmed, and EVERY METAL ON THE BOARD FELL - zinc -2.27%, nickel -2.06%, aluminium -2.05%, copper -0.96%, lead -0.29%. THE DOLLAR INDEX IS FIRMER AGAIN AT 99.12 ON THE 12-SEPTEMBER REFERENCE BOARD AND THE FEDERAL RESERVE DECIDES ON 16-SEPTEMBER. This risk is deliberately kept separate from the aluminium-specific rows because it moves the whole complex at once and is therefore not diversifiable within metals.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO DOWN, AND THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL TREND CHANGE ON THIS PAGE THIS RUN, SO THE REASONING IS SET OUT IN FULL RATHER THAN ASSERTED. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS GEOPOLITICAL ESCALATION AROUND GULF SUPPLY AND ITS ROUTES. IT IS LOWERED ON A CHANGE IN THE CATEGORY OF EVIDENCE, NOT ON A CHANGE IN THE PHYSICAL SITUATION. For weeks this page carried a single unconfirmed report of an Iran-Oman arrangement at deliberately low confidence and explicitly refused to upgrade it merely because time had passed. THAT REPORT IS NOW DATED, SPECIFIC AND CARRIED BY MORE THAN ONE OUTLET: on 07-September Iran said an agreement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping was days away, after more than three weeks of talks covering proposed inbound and outbound routes, the security and sovereignty of both states, and a proposed joint coordination centre; a separate 26-August report states a temporary maritime route had already been agreed. THREE QUALIFICATIONS ARE CARRIED RATHER THAN BURIED. NOTHING IS SIGNED. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED, and full reopening is reported as conditional on the United States fulfilling commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed. AND THE ESCALATION FACTS ARE NOT DELETED - Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait, the United States said it sank five Iranian tankers, the Houthis hold Mocha and Bab el-Mandeb transits are down about 24%. THE TREND MOVES ONE STEP, NOT TO CLEAR, BECAUSE AN ARRANGEMENT THAT TIGHTENS IRANIAN CONTROL OVER THE WATERWAY IS NOT THE SAME THING AS A REOPENING.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM FLAT TO DOWN ON THE LARGEST BLOCK OF NEW DATED EVIDENCE THIS RUN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK PROPAGATING INTO SMELTER MARGIN, AND THE EVIDENCE NOW POINTS AWAY FROM IT IN FOUR SEPARATE SERIES. Dated 12-September: Guinean bauxite shipments 4.33 Mt in the 21-27 August week, up 28.4% year on year; 2026 Guinea FOB bauxite forecast $34-46/dmt against $40-65/dmt in 2025; Australian FOB $39.15/wmt in FY26 against $51.48/wmt in FY25; Asian alumina exports 7.05 Mt in H1-2026, up 27.36% year on year; India's alumina trade surplus 1.72 Mt, nearly quadruple a year earlier. THE MOST RECENT DATED ALUMINA TRADE, 50,000 mt AT $353.50/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA ON 11-SEPTEMBER, IS ESSENTIALLY FLAT ON A FIVE-WEEK-OLD MARK, WHICH IS CONSISTENT: TONNES MOVING WITHOUT PRICES MOVING IS WHAT SURPLUS LOOKS LIKE. THE ONE PIECE OF CONTRARY EVIDENCE IS KEPT VISIBLE AND IS THE REASON THE IMPACT RATING STAYS HIGH: Chinese ten-port bauxite inventories fell 1,610,000 tonnes week on week in the 11-September survey, thinning the buffer against a Guinea interruption, and Alunorte runs at full capacity only on an agreement publicly described as temporary.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT FLAT ON NO NEW DATED INPUT, AND IT REMAINS THE MOST GENUINELY TWO-SIDED JUDGEMENT ON THIS PAGE. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT REGIONAL PREMIA RESET SHARPLY LOWER AND DRAG REALISED DELIVERED VALUES WITH THEM. Nothing newer than the 11-September consensus has printed, so the pending Q4 Japanese range stays at $280-310 and is NOT tightened on a repeated reading. WHAT ARRIVED WAS CORROBORATION RATHER THAN MOVEMENT: a second publisher on 12-September restates the $310-325/t producer offer for October-December as down 18-22% on the $395/t Q3 settlement. THAT RAISES CONFIDENCE IN THE UPPER BOUND WITHOUT MOVING IT, WHICH IS WHY THE TREND DOES NOT CHANGE. A settlement near the $280-290 consensus would be a fall of roughly 28% in a single quarter.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE INVENTORY ARGUMENT UNDERPINNING THE BULL CASE STOPS WORKING. The last published warehouse line drew 250 tonnes to 244,100, a FIFTH consecutive decline, and it did so on a session in which flat price fell 2.06%. METAL DID NOT COME BACK TO THE WAREHOUSE ON A SHARPLY LOWER PRICE, which is the opposite of what a failing inventory argument looks like. NO NEW WAREHOUSE REPORT EXISTS FOR A WEEKEND AND NONE HAS BEEN ESTIMATED, so the risk is held rather than lowered further - a carried series is not a confirming one. The stock axis has been re-checked this run and continues to bracket the series with roughly 9,100 tonnes of headroom to the floor.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT DOWN, BUT WITH A DELIBERATE NOTE THAT THE EVIDENCE IS AGEING RATHER THAN ACCUMULATING. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS THAT THE CURVE SIGNAL IS TOO SMALL OR TOO FRAGILE TO ACT ON IN EITHER DIRECTION. It was lowered on 12-September because the signal had been tested in the harshest available way and held: flat price fell 2.06% and the backwardation narrowed by ONE DOLLAR, from $25.00 to $24.00, while stocks drew again. THAT TEST STANDS AND IS NOT RE-EARNED BY THE PASSAGE OF A WEEKEND. THE SIGNAL HAS NOW GONE THREE CALENDAR DAYS WITHOUT A FURTHER TEST, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT LOWERED FURTHER. Monday 14-September at 13:20 London is the test, and a flattening or flipping spread would reverse this row immediately.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. HELD AT UP. THE EU IMPORT BAN ON RUSSIAN PRIMARY ALUMINIUM TAKES EFFECT ON 31-DECEMBER-2026, ABOUT FIFTEEN WEEKS AWAY, AND IT IS THE LARGEST SCHEDULED STRUCTURAL EVENT ON THIS PAGE'S HORIZON. Europe must replace those tonnes from somewhere and the two candidate sources both have problems: Gulf metal is the subject of the chokepoint question above, and European restart capacity depends on power economics. THE POWER SIDE IMPROVED MARGINALLY THIS RUN - European gas eased to EUR 79.52/MWh - AND THAT IS THE VARIABLE SLOVALCO'S GUIDED Q4 RESTART OF ITS FIRST 75,000 TONNES IS MOST EXPOSED TO. A SINGLE WEEK OF CHEAPER GAS DOES NOT UNDERWRITE A SMELTER RESTART AND THE RISK IS NOT LOWERED ON IT.

RE-ASSESSED 13-SEPTEMBER. LOWERED FROM UP TO DOWN, AND THE EVIDENCE IS DIRECT RATHER THAN INFERRED. THE RISK AS WRITTEN IS SOURCE-DATA INTEGRITY: that the published price feed this page depends on is stale, cached or internally inconsistent without saying so. IT WAS RAISED ON 12-SEPTEMBER WHEN THE GERMAN OVERVIEW CARRIED THE 11-SEPTEMBER BOARD AND THE ENGLISH OVERVIEW STILL SHOWED 10-SEPTEMBER. BOTH WERE RE-REQUESTED THIS MORNING AND BOTH NOW CARRY 11-SEPTEMBER, IDENTICAL LINE FOR LINE ACROSS ALL SIX METALS, ALL SIX STOCK LINES AND ALL THREE FX FIXINGS. The divergence has closed. THE RISK IS LOWERED, NOT CLEARED, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: the same source has now lagged in BOTH languages within six weeks - English on 04-August, German on 12-September - so the cross-check remains mandatory every run and the per-metal daily tables remain the arbiter. A RESOLVED OUTAGE IS NOT A RELIABLE SOURCE.

THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
